clue.text: Fraudster, initially careless, forgetting small limp

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows, and nothing more
forgetting something means leaving it out, so the abbreviation that follows is dropped

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
careless work is sloppy
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A con artist who has got careless and lets small details slip.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'Fraudster' look like the subject, but only its first letter is used; 'careless' supplies the main body once the small one is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limp hangs loose without stiffness, which is exactly what a floppy hat or ear does.

clue.text: Predicted luggage emptied in part of ship

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is cleared out, leaving just the outer letters

blocks.note: forecast as a past tense means foretold
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Baggage that was expected to go missing in some part of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle, often written fo'c'sle, is the forward section of a ship below the bow deck.

clue.text: Newspaper belonging to senior gangster

indicators.note: belonging to means contained within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A paper owned by a top mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a publication that speaks for a party or group, as in a party's official mouthpiece.

clue.text: Illustrations about one system of exercises

indicators.note: about means around, so these pictures wrap around the next piece

blocks.note: plates are full-page pictures in a book
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Diagrams showing a single workout routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a regime of controlled body-conditioning movements devised by Joseph Pilates.

clue.text: Had a fight cancelled

blocks.note: first meaning: brawled or tussled
second meaning: abandoned or thrown out as useless

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a fight that got called off, but the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is informally to brawl, and also to discard a plan, so the past tense covers both senses.

clue.text: Crusty representation of Saturn on cake

indicators.note: a representation is a rendering or depiction, so the letters are made into a fresh form

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A planet piped in icing on a cake with a crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusty' suggests pastry and cake, but it is the definition in its sense of grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusty person is irritable and gruff, the same bad-tempered sense as quarrelsome and grouchy.

clue.text: A fool, admitting offence, causing laughter

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the wrong is taken inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a mug is a gullible person
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A clown confessing to a misdeed gets everyone giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug for a dupe is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing is funny and entertaining, provoking smiles and laughs.

clue.text: Write slight, unfinished article, making point?

indicators.note: unfinished means the ending is missing, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to pen is to write
a slight is an insult or snub
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Penning a short, half-done article to make an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like making a point in an essay; the question mark flags that it is a geographical point.
explanation.definitionFit: A point of land jutting into the sea is a headland, and a peninsula is a larger version of one.

clue.text: Give up work to follow northward road

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters come backwards
to follow places the work after the road

blocks.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road
op. is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Quitting one's job to head up the road north.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a habit or class is to abandon it, the same as giving it up.

clue.text: Entertain like a monarch with energy

blocks.note: regal means kingly or queenly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Laying on lavish hospitality as a king would, with plenty of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to entertain them, with stories or a lavish meal, a fairly close synonym.

clue.text: Suggestion from union newly filled with purpose

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters are made over afresh into a different order
filled with means another piece is packed inside this one

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A proposal emerging from a freshly formed trade union with a clear purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' reads as a trade union, but it is just letters to be rearranged; 'end' for purpose is a common crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint or insinuation, a kind of suggestion rather than a plain statement.

clue.text: Five in one group joined by capital songwriter

indicators.note: in places the number inside the following word
joined by means the next piece is attached alongside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring
V is the Roman numeral five
Berlin is the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: Five musicians in one band team up with a top-notch composer.
explanation.walkthrough: V sits inside RING after its first letter, preceded by I. Irving Berlin wrote White Christmas and many other standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was a prolific American popular composer and lyricist, one of the great writers of songs.

clue.text: Business with land involving severe anxiety

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
a land or country
severe, strict

explanation.surface: A company dealing in property causes a great deal of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business with land' reads as a property firm; in fact the business is just its abbreviation, and the land is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is alarm or dismay, a sudden anxious confusion, so it stands for the noun anxiety.

clue.text: Anger after referring to saucy old range

indicators.note: after puts the anger at the end, following the other pieces

blocks.note: re means concerning or referring to
pert means cheeky or saucy
O is the abbreviation for old
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury aroused by a collection of risqué old material.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the anger first, but 'after' sends IRE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's repertoire is the full range of pieces they are ready to perform, their stock of material.

clue.text: Friends, coming round, put up with knockabout comedy

indicators.note: coming round suggests turning about, so the word is read from the other end

blocks.note: pals are friends
to stick something is to tolerate it, as in 'I can't stick him'

explanation.surface: Mates drop in, and you endure their boisterous clowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' meaning tolerate is mainly British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is broad physical comedy of pratfalls and pies in the face, the same thing as knockabout humour.

clue.text: Brass, a lot, playing Fleetwood Mac tune

indicators.note: playing suggests performing with the letters, rearranging them freely

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A large brass section performing a hit by a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Albatross is Fleetwood Mac's 1968 instrumental, a UK number one.
explanation.definitionFit: Albatross is the title of a famous instrumental recording by the band Fleetwood Mac.

clue.text: Measure uniform in good time

indicators.note: in places one piece within the following word

blocks.note: G is a common abbreviation for good
an age is a long period of time
Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for U

explanation.surface: Sizing a uniform in good time, before it is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside AGE, which follows G; 'in good time' looks like a stock phrase but splits up.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to measure or estimate an amount, so the verb matches measure.

clue.text: Projecting parts, large, mostly overweight

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
obese means seriously overweight

explanation.surface: Body parts that stick out on someone large and heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobes are rounded projecting parts, like an earlobe or the lobes of a leaf or lung.

clue.text: Branch of study for citizen

blocks.note: first meaning: a school or university discipline
second meaning: a person owing allegiance to a monarch or state

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a civics course; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Maths or history is a school discipline, and a British national is called one of the Crown's subjects.

clue.text: Pests, not very restricted by barrier, start to grow

indicators.note: not very tells you to remove the abbreviation for very from the word before
restricted by means hemmed in by the next word, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: a gate is a barrier across an opening
vermin are pests such as rats and mice

explanation.surface: Pests held back by a fence before they can breed and spread.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the abbreviation for very, so VERMIN loses it to leave ERMIN, which goes inside GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To germinate is for a seed to sprout, which is beginning to develop into a plant.

clue.text: Copy? Some acclaim it at exhibition

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word through to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Asking whether a work praised at a gallery show is merely a forgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce something, which is what copying does.

clue.text: Recreation of scene with sad value a bit before verse by soldier?

indicators.note: sad in the sense of sorry or poor quality suggests the letters are in a bad state and need reordering
before places the rearranged letters ahead of what follows
by means next to, so the last piece sits alongside

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
V is the abbreviation for verse
a soldier ant, as in the insect caste

explanation.surface: A poor attempt by a soldier to re-stage a scene, with a little bit of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a soldier here is the insect. A tableau vivant is a scene posed silently by costumed people, like a living painting.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means living picture: actors hold still to reproduce a famous painting or historical moment.

clue.text: Cool under cooker once more

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places this piece below the next one

blocks.note: an Aga is a brand of heavy cast-iron range cooker
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Chilling something beneath the stove a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British range cooker found in many country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, so it is a straight synonym of once more.

clue.text: Frustrate lawyer with silence

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Thwarting an attorney by refusing to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to ruin or thwart them, which frustrates them.

clue.text: Sailor with cargo finally left, carrying meat most importantly

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before
carrying means holding something within, so the meat goes inside

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual sailor
the last letter of this word
veal is calf meat
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A seaman whose ship's freight has finally gone, but who still has his meat on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb meaning departed, but it is the abbreviation; together with the cargo's last letter it wraps around the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means first and foremost, the thing that matters before everything else.

clue.text: Much occupying one when about to make expedition

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pair before it is read backwards
occupying means taking up space inside another piece

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
as in 'as he arrived', meaning when
far as in 'far better', meaning much

explanation.surface: Lots of people taking part in something when it is about to become a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns round the pair of one and when together, and 'much' goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland expedition, traditionally in East Africa, to hunt or watch wild animals.

clue.text: Man with cheers interrupting broadcast isn't lacking confidence

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
interrupting means breaking into the middle of something

blocks.note: a man is a he
taken as written, then rearranged
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A man heckled by cheering during a broadcast is not short of self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the man isn't lacking confidence, but the definition is just 'lacking confidence'; 'isn't' is fodder, not a negation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant falters and holds back from uncertainty, which is lacking confidence.

clue.text: Plan that is for small-minded person

blocks.note: to mean to do something is to plan or intend it
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: Scheming something for a petty individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is an informal word for a petty, ungenerous or spiteful person.
